cls: Recombinant human IgG1 monoclonal antibody - VEGFR2 antagonist (antiangiogenic)
pharm: Antineoplastic agent (vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 inhibitor)
tags: Boxed warning - hemorrhage, GI perforation, impaired wound healing
quick: 8 mg/kg or 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks depending on indication/regimen
Intravenous infusion; not related to meals
Can cause fetal harm based on mechanism; avoid - use contraception
Advise not to breastfeed during and after therapy
No clinically important PK differences; no specific adjustment described
Use caution in Child-Pugh B/C (worsening of encephalopathy/ascites)
No specific interaction described in labeling
Bleeding, BP, proteinuria, wound healing, infusion reactions, thyroid
summary: Ramucirumab is a recombinant human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that antagonizes vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2), used to treat advanced gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, metastatic colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma (as a single agent or with chemotherapy/erlotinib). It is given by intravenous infusion every 2 weeks at 8 mg/kg or 10 mg/kg depending on the indication. It carries a BOXED WARNING for hemorrhage (including severe and fatal gastrointestinal hemorrhage), gastrointestinal perforation, and impaired wound healing - withhold before elective surgery and discontinue permanently for severe bleeding, GI perforation, or wound-healing complications. Additional risks include arterial thromboembolism, hypertension, infusion reactions, proteinuria/nephrotic syndrome, reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome, and thyroid dysfunction.
indications: Advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma after fluoropyrimidine- or platinum-containing chemotherapy (single agent or with paclitaxel)
Metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 (L858R) mutations, first-line in combination with erlotinib
Metastatic non-small cell lung cancer after platinum-based chemotherapy, in combination with docetaxel
Metastatic colorectal cancer with progression on prior bevacizumab, oxaliplatin, and a fluoropyrimidine, in combination with FOLFIRI
Hepatocellular carcinoma (as a single agent) in patients previously treated with sorafenib

dosage.d: 8 mg/kg every 2 weeks as a single agent or with weekly paclitaxel
dosage.n: Premedicate with IV H1 antagonist before each infusion

dosage.d: 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks with daily erlotinib
dosage.n: For EGFR exon 19 del / exon 21 L858R mutations

dosage.d: 10 mg/kg on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle prior to docetaxel
8 mg/kg every 2 weeks prior to FOLFIRI

admin: For intravenous infusion only - do NOT administer as IV push or bolus

Premedicate before each infusion with an IV histamine-1 receptor antagonist; for patients with prior Grade 1-2 infusion reactions, also premedicate with dexamethasone (or equivalent) and acetaminophen
Dilute and infuse per labeling; monitor during and after infusion for reactions
Withhold for 28 days prior to elective surgery and do not resume for at least 2 weeks after major surgery and until adequate wound healing
Withhold for severe hypertension, urine protein >=2 g/24 h, or significant infusion reactions per labeling
moa: Ramucirumab is a recombinant human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that specifically binds vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) and blocks binding of the VEGFR ligands VEGF-A, VEGF-C, and VEGF-D. This inhibits ligand-stimulated activation of VEGFR2, thereby inhibiting ligand-induced proliferation and migration of human endothelial cells and blocking tumor angiogenesis.

absolute: No contraindications are listed in the prescribing information
relative: Active or high risk of serious bleeding; recent hemoptysis
Recent major surgery, non-healing wounds, or planned elective surgery
Child-Pugh B or C cirrhosis (risk of hepatic decompensation)
monitor: Infusion reactions, thyroid function, and neurologic symptoms (RPLS)

preg: Based on its mechanism of action, ramucirumab can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman, as VEGFR2 signaling is critical to embryo-fetal development and angiogenesis. There are no human data. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk; women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during and for a period after treatment per labeling.
lact: There is no information on the presence of ramucirumab in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for a period after the last dose.
renal: No clinically important pharmacokinetic differences were observed across renal function (CLcr 15-89 mL/min); the labeling does not specify a renal dose adjustment.
hepatic: No clinically important PK differences were seen with mild or moderate hepatic impairment based on bilirubin/AST. However, clinical deterioration (encephalopathy, ascites) has occurred in patients with Child-Pugh B or C cirrhosis - use only if the benefit outweighs the risk and monitor closely.

major: Other antiangiogenic agents or anticoagulants/antiplatelets (additive bleeding risk)
moderate: Chemotherapy partners (paclitaxel, docetaxel, FOLFIRI) and erlotinib - additive toxicities per combination labeling
minor: No formal small-molecule pharmacokinetic drug-interaction concerns established for a monoclonal antibody
interactions.alcohol: No specific alcohol interaction is described in the labeling.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor blood pressure and urine protein (dipstick/24-hour); assess thyroid function during therapy.

serious: Hemorrhage including severe and fatal gastrointestinal hemorrhage
emergency: Hypertensive crisis or RPLS (severe headache, seizure, vision change, altered consciousness)

monitoring: Signs of bleeding and gastrointestinal perforation; discontinue permanently for severe events
Blood pressure before each infusion and treat hypertension; withhold for severe hypertension
Urine protein - monitor and withhold/discontinue per proteinuria thresholds
Wound healing around any surgery; hold before/after surgery
Infusion reactions, thyroid function, and neurologic signs of RPLS
counsel: Report any bleeding (black/bloody stools, vomiting blood, severe nosebleeds, coughing up blood) or severe abdominal pain immediately
Tell your team about any planned surgery or dental procedure - this drug must be stopped beforehand
Your blood pressure and urine will be checked regularly
Report chest pain, weakness/numbness, trouble speaking, severe headache, seizures, or vision changes urgently
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed during treatment
pk: Acts via VEGFR2 blockade; steady-state concentrations achieved at approximately 12 weeks
Achieved at end of the intravenous infusion
Every-2-week dosing maintains exposure (mean clearance ~0.015 L/hour)
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C; do not freeze or shake; protect from light (per labeling)
pearls: BOXED WARNING: hemorrhage (including severe and fatal GI hemorrhage), gastrointestinal perforation, and impaired wound healing - discontinue permanently for severe bleeding or GI perforation
Withhold for 28 days before elective surgery; do not resume until >=2 weeks after major surgery and wound healing is adequate
Antiangiogenic class risks: arterial thromboembolism, hypertension, proteinuria/nephrotic syndrome, and RPLS
It is a biologic (monoclonal antibody) - see pearls; this monograph is based on the FDA prescribing information (CYRAMZA)
Caution in Child-Pugh B/C cirrhosis due to risk of hepatic decompensation
missed: Ramucirumab is administered in a clinical setting on a fixed schedule; a missed or delayed infusion should be rescheduled by the oncology team rather than self-managed. Dose modifications (withhold/reduce) are determined by the clinician based on toxicity.
overdose: There are no data on overdose with ramucirumab. In the event of overdose, monitor for signs or symptoms of adverse reactions and institute appropriate symptomatic and supportive treatment; there is no specific antidote.
